property_summary: For any non-zero address passed to transferOwnership by the current owner, the call succeeds; the mutant removes the check and thus allows transferring to the zero address which should be disallowed (the reference will revert when newOwner==address(0) but the mutant will succeed).

For any caller who is the current owner, calling transferOwnership with any address should revert iff the new owner is the zero address in the reference; the mutant allows setting owner to zero (succeeds) for some input (newOwner == address(0)).

For any caller that is the current owner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) must revert iff newOwner == address(0); the buggy mutant removes the require and thus allows a transfer to address(0) (succeeds) for that input.

For any caller who is the current owner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) either succeeds and sets owner to newOwner when newOwner != address(0), or reverts when newOwner == address(0); the mutant removes the revert on newOwner==address(0) and therefore for some fuzzed newOwner (the zero address) the mutant succeeds while the reference reverts.

For any caller that is the current owner, transferOwnership(newOwner) must either revert when newOwner == address(0) (reference) or succeed otherwise; the mutant removes the zero-address check so there exists an input newOwner == address(0) where the reference reverts but the mutant succeeds — we express this as: when the current owner calls transferOwnership with an arbitrary address, the call succeeds iff that address is non-zero (reference always enforces this), and the mutant will violate this by allowing success for newOwner == address(0).
Only the contract owner can change the rewardDistributor (setRewardDistributor) — i.e., a call to setRewardDistributor by the current rewardDistributor must revert unless it is also the owner.

property_summary: Only the contract owner (not an arbitrary non-owner) can successfully call setRewardDistributor; calls from non-owners must revert.
Calls to setRewardDistributor by any caller other than the contract owner always revert (i.e., only the owner can successfully call setRewardDistributor).
If the caller is the contract owner, calling setRewardDistributor should not revert.
If msg.sender equals the contract owner then calling setRewardDistributor(...) does not revert.

After any call to addReward(token) by the contract owner, the rewardDistributor remains unchanged (still the original distributor); the mutant allows rewardDistributor to be changed by the current distributor and thus can cause rewardDistributor to differ after addReward for some inputs.
